reference_drawer.title: 📖 Systematic Factor Listing Guide
reference_drawer.description: The 4 Universal Sign Rules for Quadratic Middle-Term Splitting:

items.rule: One positive and one negative (+, -). Larger magnitude is positive.
One positive and one negative (+, -). Larger magnitude is negative.

concepts.title: 1. What is a Systematic Factor Pair?
concepts.subtitle: Listing All Divisors Without Guessing
concepts.summary: To list all factor pairs of integer N, test natural numbers starting from 1 up to √N.

points.text: The √N Stopping Rule: You only need to test divisors up to √N. Once the quotient becomes smaller than the divisor, all pairs are found.
Systematic Increment: Test 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... sequentially so no pair is ever missed.

concepts.trap: Do not jump between random numbers; always test 1, 2, 3, 4 in ascending order.

concepts.title: 2. The 4 Quadratic Sign Signatures
concepts.subtitle: Determining Signs Before Finding Numbers
concepts.summary: The signs of product ac and sum b uniquely determine whether factors are both positive, both negative, or mixed.

points.text: ac Positive: Factors have the SAME sign (matching the sign of b).
ac Negative: Factors have OPPOSITE signs (larger factor takes the sign of b).

concepts.trap: Always determine the signs of the two factors before picking numeric magnitudes.

concepts.title: 3. The 3-Column Factor Table Method
concepts.subtitle: Guaranteed Middle-Term Split Algorithm
concepts.summary: Construct a 3-column table: [Factor Pair] → [Sum] → [Match Target b?].

points.text: Column 2: Compute the signed sum of each pair.
Column 3: Stop immediately when the sum matches coefficient b.

concepts.trap: Never guess randomly for large products (like 84 or 120); always write the table.

concepts.title: 4. Grouping and Factoring GCF
concepts.subtitle: Pairwise Common Binomial Extraction
concepts.summary: Group the 4 terms into two pairs and factor out the greatest common factor from each pair.

points.text: First Pair: Factor out numerical GCF and x (e.g. 2x² - 6x = 2x(x - 3)).

concepts.formula: Ax(x - k) + B(x - k) = (x - k)(Ax + B)
concepts.trap: If the third term is negative, remember to factor out a negative sign so the binomials match.
